title: Microsoft Purview DLP: block named external domains or users from SharePoint and OneDrive files
notes: claim 47: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the impact rationale says only block-listed external people are affected, although Microsoft's rule notes also describe blocking people in neither list. The briefing also overstates the required policy locations and omits the owner and last-modifier exceptions when describing the PowerShell All scope. Roadmap facts and the reported public-preview limitations are supported.

claims.claim: Roadmap 557191 describes Microsoft Purview DLP policies blocking SharePoint and OneDrive file access for specific external domains or individual users.
claims.quote: With this enhancement, admins can configure DLP policies that block file access for specific external domains or individual users.

claims.quote: Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list. On the Customize advanced DLP rules page, select + Create rule.
claims.fix: Expand the abbreviated route to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations > Block users from receiving email or accessing shared SharePoint, OneDrive > Block access for specific external domains or users'. The source's numbered variant steps also omit the Block users grouping, so its omission alone is not evidence of an unusable route. Use https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule BlockAccessScope offers All, PerUser and PerAnonymousUser for blocking everyone, external users and Anyone-link users respectively.
claims.quote: All: Blocks access to everyone except the owner and the last modifier. PerUser: Blocks access to external users. PerAnonymousUser: Blocks access to people through the "Anyone with the link" option in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with '`New-DlpComplianceRule` documents `-BlockAccessScope` values of All (everyone except the owner and last modifier), PerUser (external users) and PerAnonymousUser (people using the Anyone with the link option in SharePoint and OneDrive); these are blocking scopes, not domain or user lists.' Use https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-dlpcompliancerule.

claims.claim: The policy must include both SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts.
claims.quote: Every policy is scoped to one or more locations, such as Exchange, SharePoint in Microsoft 365, Teams, and Devices.
claims.fix: Replace 'The policy must include the SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts locations' with 'Select the SharePoint sites and/or OneDrive accounts locations that you intend this policy to cover.' The scenario selects both to cover both workloads, not as a universal requirement. The scope rule is at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy and this action's supported locations are at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-policy-reference.

claims.claim: Only external people on a block list notice the change when a matching file stops opening.
claims.quote: rationale: "only external people on a block list notice"; Risk assessment: "users in neither list are blocked by default where a file matches both kinds of rule".
claims.fix: Replace the factual portion of the impact rationale with 'Compliance admins configure it. External collaborators can notice when a matching file stops opening; Learn notes that users in neither list are also blocked by default when a file matches both an allow rule and a block rule. User notifications are not supported.' Keep the low impact judgement; the correction concerns the factual limitation, not the rating. See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external.
